This integration connects Gladys to your **Tailscale** network (your
"tailnet"): every machine of the tailnet — a server, a NAS, a phone, a subnet
router — becomes a Gladys device that shows whether it is online, whether a
Tailscale update is waiting, and when its key expires.

It reads the tailnet through the **Tailscale API, in the cloud**
(`api.tailscale.com`). Nothing needs to be installed on your machines, and
Gladys does not have to be on the tailnet itself.

Requires Gladys 5.3 or later.

## Before you begin

You need to be an **admin** of the tailnet (Owner, Admin or IT admin role) to
create the credentials below.

The integration signs in with one of these:

| Method           | Where to create it                                                           | Expires             |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| API access token | [Settings → Keys](https://login.tailscale.com/admin/settings/keys)           | after 1 to 90 days  |
| OAuth client     | [Settings → OAuth clients](https://login.tailscale.com/admin/settings/oauth) | never (recommended) |

### API access token

1. Open [Settings → Keys](https://login.tailscale.com/admin/settings/keys) in
   the Tailscale admin console.
2. Under **API access tokens**, click **Generate access token**, give it a
   description ("Gladys") and an expiry.
3. Copy the token (`tskey-api-…`): Tailscale shows it only once.

When the token expires, the integration shows "Tailscale refused the
credentials" and the devices turn **unreachable**: generate a new one and
paste it in the configuration.

### OAuth client (recommended)

An OAuth client never expires, and you choose exactly what it may do.

1. Open [Settings → OAuth clients](https://login.tailscale.com/admin/settings/oauth).
2. Click **Generate OAuth client**.
3. Tick the **Devices → Core** scope:
   - **Read** is enough to watch the machines;
   - **Write** is also needed to turn a machine's key expiry on or off from
     Gladys.
4. Copy the **Client ID** and the **Client secret** (`tskey-client-…`): the
   secret is shown only once.

## Configuration

1. Open the **Configuration** tab of the integration.
2. Pick the **Sign-in method** and fill in its fields:
   - API access token: paste it in **API access token**;
   - OAuth client: paste **OAuth client ID** and **OAuth client secret**.
3. **Tailnet**: leave `-`, the tailnet of the credentials. Only change it if
   your token can reach several tailnets: put the tailnet ID shown in
   **Settings → General** of the admin console.
4. **Refresh interval**: how often the tailnet is read, every 60 seconds by
   default (30 seconds minimum). Each refresh is a single request, whatever
   the number of machines.
5. **Key expiry warning**: how many days before a key expires the machine is
   flagged (14 by default).
6. **Include machines shared with you**: machines another tailnet shares into
   yours are hidden by default, since you do not manage them.
7. Save, then click **Test the connection**: it says how many machines the
   integration sees.
8. Open the **Discovery** tab and add the machines you want to follow.

## What you get

Each machine becomes a device with four features:

| Feature             | Meaning                                                                           |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Online              | The machine is connected to the tailnet right now                                 |
| Update available    | A newer Tailscale version exists for this machine                                 |
| Key expiry          | Days left before its key expires (not updated while key expiry is off)            |
| Key expiry disabled | The switch of the admin console's **Disable key expiry** menu — you can change it |

Turning **Key expiry disabled** on from Gladys is the same as **Disable key
expiry** in the admin console: the machine will never have to sign in again.
It needs an API token, or an OAuth client with the **Devices → Core: Write**
scope.

Every device shows a **cloud** badge while the Tailscale API answers, and
**unreachable** when it does not: the values shown are then the last ones
read.

The machines are matched on their Tailscale ID: renaming a machine in the
admin console keeps its device and its history in Gladys.

## Scenes

The integration adds its own cards to the scene editor, under the
**Integrations** category.

### Triggers

- **Machine online or offline** — a machine connected to or disconnected from
  the tailnet. Optionally pick the machine and the new state; left empty, any
  machine and any change match. Variables: `device_name`, `state` (`online` or
  `offline`), `ip`, `last_seen`.
- **New machine in the tailnet** — a machine joined the tailnet. Filter on
  **Approval** to be told only about machines waiting for approval (with
  device approval turned on). Variables: `device_name`, `authorization`
  (`authorized` or `pending`), `os`, `user`, `ip`.
- **Tailscale update available** — a newer Tailscale client is available for
  a machine. Variables: `device_name`, `client_version`.
- **Key expiring soon** — a machine's key enters the warning period of the
  configuration. Variables: `device_name`, `days_left`, `expires`.

The following actions of the scene read a variable as
`{{triggerEvent.data.device_name}}`.

Each trigger fires **once per change**, when the integration notices it (at
the refresh interval). Starting the integration fires nothing: it first takes
note of the tailnet as it is.

Example: _when a machine goes offline, send me a message "\{\{triggerEvent.data.device_name\}\} is offline"_.

### Actions

- **Refresh the tailnet** — reads every machine now. Returns `machine_count`,
  `online_count` and `offline_count`.
- **Read a machine's status** — returns `name`, `online`, `ip`, `last_seen`,
  `os`, `client_version`, `update_available`, `key_expiry_disabled` and
  `key_expiry_days` (`-1` when the key never expires), for the conditions and
  messages that follow.
- **Change a machine's key expiry** — turns key expiry off for a machine, or
  back on. Returns `key_expiry_disabled`.

## Dashboard

Add the **Tailscale network** widget to a dashboard. It shows:

- how many machines are online and offline;
- whether the API answers, when the tailnet was last read, how many machines
  have an update waiting, a key about to expire or are waiting for approval;
- a list of machines, with a badge for the most pressing problem. Tap a
  machine to see its addresses, owner, tags and key expiry date, with a link
  to its page in the admin console.

Settings of each widget:

- **Machines listed**: those that need attention (default), the offline ones
  only, or all of them;
- **Rows**: how many machines the list shows (0 to 8).

The **Refresh** button reads the tailnet at once; **Admin console** opens the
Tailscale admin console.

## Troubleshooting

| Message                                            | What to do                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No Tailscale credentials                           | Fill in the fields of the chosen sign-in method                                  |
| Tailscale refused the credentials                  | The token expired or was revoked, or the OAuth client is wrong: create a new one |
| Access denied: the token lacks the "devices" scope | Give the OAuth client the **Devices → Core** scope                               |
| Tailnet not found                                  | Put `-` back in **Tailnet**, or the exact ID from **Settings → General**         |
| Tailscale limits the requests                      | Raise the refresh interval                                                       |
| The Tailscale API cannot be reached from Gladys    | Check the internet access of the Gladys host (`api.tailscale.com`, HTTPS)        |

A machine shows **offline** while it works? It is offline for Tailscale: the
client is stopped, logged out, or its key expired. The admin console shows the
same thing.

The integration logs everything it does: open the integration logs in Gladys.
It never logs a token or a secret.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Tailscale asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Getting started | `section` | No | The integration reads your tailnet through the Tailscale API, in the cloud: nothing to install on your machines. Create an API access token (Settings → Keys, it expires after 90 days at most) or, better, an OAuth client with the "devices:core" scope (Settings → OAuth clients, it never expires), then paste it below. |
| Sign-in method | `select` | Yes |  |
| API access token | `secret` | No | Only for the "API access token" method. |
| OAuth client ID | `string` | No | Only for the "OAuth client" method. |
| OAuth client secret | `secret` | No |  |
| Tailnet | `string` | No | Leave "-" for the tailnet of the token. Otherwise its ID, shown in Settings → General. |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | No | How often the tailnet is read, in seconds. One request per refresh, whatever the number of machines. |
| Key expiry warning (days) | `number` | No | A machine whose key expires within this many days fires the "Key expiring soon" trigger. |
| Include machines shared with you | `boolean` | No | Machines another tailnet shares into yours. Hidden by default: they are not yours to manage. |

## How to install Tailscale in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Tailscale appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/prohand/gladys-tailscale:1.1.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/prohand/gladys-tailscale](https://github.com/prohand/gladys-tailscale).

Tailscale requires Gladys `>=5.3.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Tailscale is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [prohand](https://github.com/prohand), not by the Gladys core team.
